records.source: Two kinds of thing are installed from a click: a segmentation backend, which is a Python package added to the running environment with ``pip`` (DINOCell and SAMCell, :data:`spacr.model_zoo.INSTALLABLE_BACKENDS`), and a Cellpose checkpoint from the model zoo, which is a file downloaded and verified by :func:`spacr.model_zoo.install`. records.label: spacr.qt.night_themes#3
records.source: THE PALETTES ARE LITERALS RATHER THAN A RECIPE. Keeping the numbers here rather than the recipe means the published colours are the reviewed colours, no solver runs at import, and ``tests/qt/test_ten_night_themes.py`` judges what actually ships.

records.translation: AS PALETAS SÃO LITERAIS, E NÃO UMA RECEITA. records.label: spacr.qt.night_themes#4
records.source: THREE COLOURS WERE MOVED OFF THE RECIPE BY MEASUREMENT, and they are the only three. records.label: spacr.qt.resonance#6
records.source: AND WHY THE FIGURE IS RECOMPUTED FROM A FIXED START EVERY FRAME RATHER THAN CARRIED FORWARD. Every ambient engine promises that a frame is a pure function of ``(seed, clock, size)`` -- ``test_the_clock_alone_decides_the _frame`` steps one engine twelve times and jumps another straight to the same clock and demands the same picture, and ``test_the_backdrop_survives_a_run`` shades the same clock on two threads and compares the bytes. A particle simulation carried forward from frame to frame satisfies neither. Relaxation from a seeded start does, costs 0.61 ms, and has the better behaviour besides: the figure always belongs to the sound that is playing now rather than to the last few seconds of it.
records.context: And why the figure is recomputed from a fixed start every frame rather than carried forward. Every ambient engine promises that a frame is a pure function of ``(seed, clock, size)`` -- ``test_the_clock_alone_decides_the _frame`` steps one engine twelve times and jumps another straight to the same clock and demands the same picture, and ``test_the_backdrop_survives_a_run`` shades the same clock on two threads and compares the bytes. A particle simulation carried forward from frame to frame satisfies neither. Relaxation from a seeded start does, costs 0.61 ms, and has the better behaviour besides: the figure always belongs to the sound that is playing now rather than to the last few seconds of it.
records.translation: E POR QUE A FIGURA É RECALCULADA A PARTIR DE UM INÍCIO FIXO A CADA QUADRO, EM VEZ DE SER LEVADA ADIANTE. Todo mecanismo ambiente promete que um quadro é função pura de ``(seed, clock, size)`` -- ``test_the_clock_alone_decides_the _frame`` avança um mecanismo doze vezes e salta outro diretamente para o mesmo relógio e exige a mesma imagem, e ``test_the_backdrop_survives_a_run`` sombreia o mesmo relógio em duas threads e compara os bytes. Uma simulação de partículas levada adiante de quadro em quadro não satisfaz nenhum dos dois. O relaxamento a partir de um início semeado satisfaz, custa 0.61 ms e ainda tem o melhor comportamento: a figura sempre pertence ao som que está tocando agora, e não aos últimos segundos dele.

records.source: THE CLOCK IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM, and it is worth saying why there is no other. ``QSoundEffect`` has no playback position to ask for, and capturing the machine's audio output is not something a scientific tool should be doing to somebody's computer. So the audio thread records the instant it called ``play()`` and the length of the loop, and the position is arithmetic. Both clocks are real time, so the two drift only by the audio device's own rate error -- tens of parts per million, a millisecond an hour -- and the loop wraps it out anyway.

So the audio thread records the instant it called ``play()`` and the length of the loop, and the position is arithmetic. Both clocks are real time, so the two drift only by the audio device's own rate error -- tens of parts per million, a millisecond an hour -- and the loop wraps it out anyway.

Então a thread de áudio registra o instante em que chamou ``play()`` e a duração do loop, e a posição é aritmética.
